provenance.written_against: the repaired q3309 statement and the final 12-case suite
provenance.note: Tier-1 entries are misconceptions a learner could plausibly hold; each carries the reason and the case expected to expose it. No mutant was added to raise a score.

input_contract.description: two strings, haystack and needle; the repaired statement permits 0 <= |s| <= 10^4 for both

mutants.description: returns the LAST occurrence instead of the first
returns how MANY times the needle occurs, not where
scans range(len(haystack) - len(needle)) and so never tries the last valid start position
treats an empty needle as 'not found' instead of returning 0
compares a window one character shorter than the needle
loop starts at index 1, skipping position 0
returns len(haystack) instead of -1 when absent
the explicit empty-needle branch is deleted
mutants.equivalence_argument: With an empty needle the loop runs over range(len(haystack) + 1) and its first comparison is haystack[0:0] == '', which is True, so it returns 0 — exactly what the deleted branch returned. The branch is documentation of the statement's rule, not behaviour, and no input can distinguish the two versions. Structural, not 'it passed the tests'.

t1-last-occurrence.why_plausible: `find` and `rfind` differ by one letter and a learner who reaches for the wrong one gets a solution that passes every single-occurrence test
t1-last-occurrence.expected_kill: case 9 (aaaa/aa) kills it first — rfind gives 2, the answer is 0. Case 10 (abcabc/abc) was the case designed to expose it and would also kill it; the earlier case simply reaches it sooner.

t1-count-not-index.why_plausible: misreading 'first occurrence' as 'occurrences'; the two agree by accident whenever the answer is 0 or 1
t1-count-not-index.expected_kill: case 1 (hello/ll): count is 1, the index is 2

t1-off-by-one-window.why_plausible: the classic missing +1: the number of start positions is len(h) - len(n) + 1, and the off-by-one is invisible unless a match sits at the very end
t1-off-by-one-window.expected_kill: case 7 (a/a): range(0) is empty, so -1 instead of 0. Case 8 would also kill it — the 10^4 match sits exactly at the excluded position

t1-empty-needle-not-found.why_plausible: the ORIGINAL statement said 1 <= |needle|, so a learner reading it never handles the empty case — this is the exact misconception the statement repair addressed

t2-comparison-inverted.expected_kill: case 1: the first window 'he' is not 'll', so it returns 0

t2-window-one-short.expected_kill: case 1: a shorter slice can never equal the needle, so -1 instead of 2

t2-scan-starts-at-one.expected_kill: case 3 (abc/a): the only match is at 0, which is skipped

t2-empty-branch-removed.expected_kill: none — behaviourally identical, documented as EQUIVALENT
